chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad and Muhammad ibn Yahya, altogether, from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Sa'd, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Muhammad ibn Sa'id ibn Ghazwan, from Ali ibn al-Hakam, from Umar ibn Aban, from Isa ibn Abu Mansur, who said:

I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'A sigh of the one concerned for us, grieving over our injustice, is a glorification (tasbih); and his thinking of our matter is worship; and his concealment of our secret is jihad in the way of Allah.'
Muhammad ibn Sa'id said to me: 'Write this in gold, for you will not write anything better than it.'

key_terms.نَفَسُ الْمَهْمُومِ: The sigh of the concerned one

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward for grieving over the Imams' injustice according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi’s chapter on Concealment (Al-Ghaybah), this hadith establishes the theological basis for 'waiting' (Intizar) as an active state of worship rather than passive inactivity. It elevates the emotional and intellectual engagement of the faithful with the Imam’s hidden status—manifested through sighing, contemplation, and guarding secrets—to the rank of major acts like jihad and tasbih, a concept central to Shia eschatology.
